items.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023
items.q: So I began, I started working with a lot of singers in town and after a while they started dying, I mean physically dying. They were Sylvia Syms, Johnny Hartman, Sammy Davis, Susannah McCorkle

ctx.x: Yeah but it happened much later. It happened after Dizzy. When I came off the road with Dizzy I got very busy in town. I started working with a lot of singers. I have — I think of myself as an accompanist and singers need to have somebody that knows how to accompany them. They don’t need to have somebody drag them along playing chords behind them. And I have like an understanding of lyrics and when I play, if I’m playing

the melody of a song somewhere I’m not just playing the melody, I’m playing the lyric. It’s very important. And singers seem to realize that when I’m working with them. So I began, I started working with a lot of singers in town and after a while they started dying, I mean physically dying. They were Sylvia Syms, Johnny Hartman, Sammy Davis, Susannah McCorkle, you know I mean they were passing away. And I said how am I — I’m never going to be able to fill that spot. The music was starting to change then also.…
I just think that’s great. You found another job you loved and had music, you loved that, so you became Mr. Gafa in the school system.
